## PCI PM registration

`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c:1031` registers the PM operations:

```c
.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops,
```

The table is defined in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1713`.

## Call chains reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

Only two PCI PM callbacks point directly to `i915_pm_suspend`:

### System suspend

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_ops.suspend
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
  -> to_i915(dev)
  -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

Relevant assignments and calls:

- `i915_driver.c:1719`
  ```c
  .suspend = i915_pm_suspend,
  ```
- `i915_driver.c:1404`
  ```c
  return i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm);
  ```
- `i915_driver.c:1120`
  ```c
  intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
  ```

### Hibernation poweroff

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_ops.poweroff
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
  -> to_i915(dev)
  -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

The `poweroff` callback reuses the same function:

- `i915_driver.c:1745`
  ```c
  .poweroff = i915_pm_suspend,
  ```

Thus, the complete set of callers of `i915_pm_suspend` from the PCI PM table is:

| PCI PM callback | Function reached |
|---|---|
| `.suspend` | `i915_pm_suspend` |
| `.poweroff` | `i915_pm_suspend` |

Both then call `i915_drm_suspend`.

## Other PCI PM callbacks

The remaining callbacks do not reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
.prepare          -> i915_pm_prepare
.suspend_late     -> i915_pm_suspend_late
.suspend_noirq    -> i915_pm_suspend_noirq
.resume_early     -> i915_pm_resume_early
.resume           -> i915_pm_resume
.complete         -> i915_pm_complete
.freeze           -> i915_pm_freeze
.freeze_late      -> i915_pm_freeze_late
.thaw_early       -> i915_pm_thaw_early
.thaw              -> i915_pm_thaw
.poweroff_late    -> i915_pm_poweroff_late
.poweroff_noirq   -> i915_pm_poweroff_noirq
.restore_early    -> i915_pm_restore_early
.restore           -> i915_pm_restore
.runtime_suspend  -> intel_runtime_suspend
.runtime_resume   -> intel_runtime_resume
```

`i915_pm_freeze()` is a special case: it independently calls `i915_drm_suspend()` at `i915_driver.c:1493`, but it does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend()`.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915` or in the searched source tree.

The runtime suspend callback is instead named:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

at `i915_driver.c:1752`.

Its chain is separate:

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend
  -> intel_runtime_suspend
  -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend
  -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend
  -> intel_gt_runtime_suspend
  -> intel_irq_suspend
  -> intel_uncore_suspend
  -> intel_display_power_suspend
```

Therefore:

- Callers of `i915_pm_suspend`: `i915_pm_ops.suspend` and `i915_pm_ops.poweroff`
- Those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`: **none**
- The actual runtime callback is `intel_runtime_suspend`, and it is not called by either `i915_pm_suspend` caller.

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The function is named `intel_display_driver_suspend`, not `intel_display_suspend`.

```text
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  |
  | struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  |
  | i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
  v
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
  |
  | struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
  | struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display
  |
  | intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
  v
intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
```

Inside `i915_drm_suspend`, `dev_priv` is also used for the non-display suspend operations:

```c
intel_power_domains_disable(display);
drm_client_dev_suspend(dev);
intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display);
intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv);
intel_hpd_cancel_work(display);
intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display);
intel_encoder_suspend_all(display);
intel_dpt_suspend(display);
i915_ggtt_suspend(to_gt(dev_priv)->ggtt);
i9xx_display_sr_save(display);
suspend_to_idle(dev_priv);
intel_opregion_suspend(display, ...);
dev_priv->suspend_count++;
intel_dmc_suspend(display);
i915_gem_drain_freed_objects(dev_priv);
```

The key pointer transformations are:

```text
struct device *kdev
  -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  -> struct drm_i915_private *i915
  -> &i915->drm
  -> to_i915(dev)
  -> struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
  -> dev_priv->display
  -> struct intel_display *display
```

`intel_display_driver_suspend()` then operates on `display`, calling:

```text
drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
  -> stores returned state in display->restore.modeset_state
flush_workqueue(display->wq.cleanup)
intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)
```
